To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) decision makers in Israel consider equity to be as important a consideration for health technology funding decisions as efficiency, and (2) equity is rarely used as an endpoint in health technology assessment.

(1) health policy makers in the Israeli National Council for the Planning and Budgeting of Health Services consider equity considerations important, and that (2) the equity considerations that they consider important do not appear to influence their decisions in practice.

(1) equity is important to policy makers, (2) equity is not currently measured in health technology assessment, (3) when equity is not measured, it is marginalised, and (4) when equity is measured, it is considered.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of quantitative methods in health technology assessment (HTA).
the question of how to make the most efficient use of limited public funds to improve population health.
how health technology assessments are used to make funding recommendations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“Equity in HTAs: what doesn’t gets measured, gets marginalise”.
equity considerations need to get more attention in HTA, but the precise way in which that should be done is not clear.
equity is not given enough weight when making health technology funding decisions in Israel and other jurisdictions, and that this needs to change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current practice of HTA is not enough to ensure that equity considerations are taken into account.
the use of quantitative equity evidence is important, and it should be used to inform the funding decisions of policy makers.
equity considerations are important in health policy, but are not given the attention they deserve in the health technology assessment of new interventions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
equity is important to policy makers, but that they need to be nudged to think more about equity when making funding decisions.
equity in health technology assessment is important, and that equity in health policy more broadly is a matter of justice.
equity considerations are important to decision makers, and that equity considerations can be measured using quantitative methods.
